title: Timed mock: URL shortener

kcs.statement: In the URL shortener mock, the requirement of non-guessable codes is separate from uniqueness: codes from a counter or sequential key ranges are unique but predictable, so they do not meet it. Codes meet it when they come from a cryptographically secure random generator, are long enough that the codes in use fill only a tiny fraction of all possible codes, and are stored with an atomic insert-if-absent that retries when a code is already taken.
In the URL shortener mock, the estimate derives write QPS, read QPS at roughly 100:1, 5-year storage and cache size, and uses them to justify a cache and a key-value store.
In the URL shortener mock, the deep dive defends code generation (key generation service vs hashing) and the redirect status plus cache headers, each with one stated trade-off.

In the URL shortener mock, the bottleneck review names the key generation service and the cache as single points of failure and gives a fix for each: replicas with failover and pre-allocated key ranges.

problem_ideas: Core activity: in one uninterrupted 45-minute attempt, submit a complete written answer for 200M new URLs a month covering requirements, estimates, API, data model, diagram, deep dive and bottlenecks; then score all seven areas in a separate review.
Variant: links must expire after 24 hours by default. Rework storage and cleanup.
Variant: the interviewer adds 'analytics per link per country'. Extend the design in 5 minutes.
Estimate the cache size if 20% of links get 80% of clicks.
Interviewer pushback: 'Why not just use auto-increment ids?' Answer it.
Present the bottleneck list with a fix for each in under 3 minutes.
